_what_this_is: Every tool BrowserAI knows of, and whether it forwards a call naming one. A tool absent from this file is a tool nobody has judged: a call naming it is refused at the BrowserAI door and never reaches Playwright. Regenerating the tools/list snapshot does NOT update this file -- that is the point.
_stop_before_you_edit_this_file: UPSTREAM-REVIEW.md. Adding a row is adopting a tool, and a row removed is a capability withdrawn.
_the_three_verdicts: allow -- forwarded to the child of the session it names, byte-identical. deny -- refused at the door AND kept out of tools/list entirely; carries why (the refusal a caller reads) and since (when it was judged). answer -- BrowserAI answers it itself; it never had a child to reach.
_an_allow_may_also_carry_why_and_since: Added 2026-09-17 with the first row judged under it. A deny MUST carry both -- the why IS the refusal a caller reads, and nothing else is -- and an allow that carries them is recording a judgement rather than producing text: why a human looked at this tool and decided a call may pass, and the day they decided. The bare allow rows were judged before this convention and are not wrong; a row with no why is a row whose reasoning is in upstream-review.json instead. Nothing enforces the convention and nothing should: an allow with a manufactured why would be worse than a bare one.
_what_the_answer_rows_actually_do: NOTHING AT RUN TIME, and saying so is the point of this line (added 2026-08-26). The `upstream` half below is load-bearing at the door: ToolVerdicts.Decide reads it on every call and a name with no row is refused. The `authored` half is not. SessionToolSurface.IsAuthored short-circuits every browserai_ name BEFORE the verdict door is reached, and SessionToolSurface.Rewrite advertises the authored tools from SessionToolSurface.Names rather than from this file -- so deleting an `answer` row changes nothing a caller can observe. What these rows ARE is build-and-test-time data: ToolVerdictTests.TheAuthoredRowsAreExactlyTheToolsBrowserAiAnswersItself holds them identical to the authored surface in BOTH directions, so the file and the code cannot drift apart, and Write-ReleaseManifest.ps1 copies the whole file into the release manifest so a rollback can see which tools a build forwarded and which upstream that was judged against. Do not read this as permission to edit them freely: a row here that disagrees with the surface is a red build, which is the whole mechanism.

browser_annotate.why: The reason is liveness rather than security: it opens the Playwright Dashboard and waits for a human to draw, it has no self-timeout — one measured call stood silent for a full 90 s and returned only when its window was closed — and the window it opens belongs to a SECOND, non-headless browser under a detached daemon that writes outside the session directory. There is no configuration in which it runs headless. An unattended run that called it would hang until it was killed. To see the page, use browser_snapshot for structure or browser_take_screenshot for pixels; both return immediately. If a human really is at the keyboard and has to mark something up, take a screenshot and have them annotate the file.

browser_emulate_media.why: Emulates CSS media features -- prefers-color-scheme, prefers-reduced-motion, forced-colors, prefers-contrast and the print/screen media type -- on the page the session already owns. It reaches nothing outside that page, it returns immediately, and it is the only way to see a site's dark mode or its print stylesheet without a second session. destructiveHint is true because it changes what the page renders, which is the same sense in which browser_navigate is destructive; nothing leaves the profile. Arrived with playwright-core 1.64.0-alpha-2026-09-17 under capability `core`, so it is in upstream's default surface.

browser_webmcp_call.why: The reason is liveness: it runs a tool the page itself supplies and waits for it with no timeout — one measured call stood silent for 45 s against a page whose tool never answered — so an unattended run that called it could hang until killed, and any page can arrange that. Use browser_webmcp_list to see what the page offers, then act on the page with the ordinary tools.
